comments.note: A03 — XSS Negative (SAFE) | gui/public/js/components/toast.js (showToast). The toast component sets message content via text.textContent = message, NOT innerHTML. Server-controlled strings in failure.error and failure.repositoryId are therefore rendered as plain text, not parsed as HTML. No XSS risk.

A02 / A09 — Credential Exposure via Toast (HIGH risk, active in upcoming credential injection WP) | src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts:127 and gui/public/js/views/project-detail.js:477. The current data flow is: gitResult.stderr -> OrchestrationRepoResult.error -> API JSON response -> browser toast textContent. This is safe today because credentials are not yet injected into URLs. HOWEVER: once the credential injection WP wires injectCredentials() into createWorkspace(), git may echo the credentialed URL in stderr (e.g., 'fatal: repository https://ghp_token@github.com/...' not found). Without sanitization, the PAT would be: (1) embedded in the API JSON response body, (2) displayed in the browser toast UI, (3) visible in browser Developer Tools NetworkTab, and (4) potentially captured by browser extensions or screen recorders. MANDATORY FIX for the credential injection WP: apply stripEmbeddedCredentials() to gitResult.stderr BEFORE assigning it to OrchestrationRepoResult.error in workspace-orchestrator.ts (line 127) and repository-orchestrator.ts (same pattern). The stripEmbeddedCredentials() utility is already implemented in src/git/git-credentials.ts. This is a blocking security prerequisite for the credential injection WP to go live.
